clue.text: Falling to win a single game and getting annoyed

blocks.note: failing to win a contest is losing it
patience is the card game played alone, called solitaire in America

explanation.surface: A card player keeps failing to win a hand and grows irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A single game' reads as one match, but it means a game for one player.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone growing irritated has run out of tolerance, the idiom for becoming cross.

clue.text: Stranded up a mountain without a drink

definitions.text: up a mountain without a drink

blocks.note: first meaning: abandoned without help

blocks.clueFragment: up a mountain without a drink
blocks.note: second meaning, taken literally: abandoned somewhere lofty and thirsty

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the idiom word by word: up a mountain is lofty, without a drink is parched.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from ships beached by the tide, meaning abandoned in a helpless position.

clue.text: Though particular, the place is in a mess

indicators.note: a mess is disorder, so these letters are jumbled into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fussy person keeps a home that is nonetheless untidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Particular and special both describe something specific or distinct from the general case.

clue.text: Opposite of a day trip?

blocks.note: surface reading: an excursion lasting a day
setter's reading: swap day for its opposite and trip for its sense of stumble

explanation.walkthrough: Trip as a stumble has a synonym, and day has an obvious opposite; put together they give the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means dusk, when darkness descends at the end of the daylight hours.

clue.text: Saucepan's ready for cooking a snipe

blocks.note: a saucepan is a pot, with its apostrophe s
a pan heated up is ready to cook with

explanation.surface: A pan heating up, ready to cook a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A snipe is a game bird, but here it is a verbal or rifle shot taken from cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A snipe is a sly attack from hiding, and a random, unaimed attack is likewise casual criticism.

clue.text: It may carry out a service on a summer afternoon

definitions.text: It may carry out a service on a summer afternoon

blocks.note: surface reading: perform a duty or a church service
setter's reading: literally bear the cups, pot and saucers of an afternoon meal outdoors

explanation.walkthrough: A tea service is a matching set of cups and pot; afternoon tea is a British light meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat board is used to bring cups, teapot and cakes out to people in the garden.

clue.text: Girl needs two keys to escape

blocks.note: a girl's name
D and E are two musical keys

explanation.surface: A young woman requires a pair of keys to get out.
explanation.walkthrough: Keys are musical keys, named by the letters A to G.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to avoid or slip away from something, so it means getting free.

clue.text: Buses — or trains

blocks.note: first meaning: long-distance road vehicles
second meaning: as a verb, instructs or tutors

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' looks like another vehicle, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names long-distance passenger vehicles; the verb means teaches or prepares an athlete.

clue.text: They help your way to the bank, providing you have a good balance

definitions.text: They help your way to the bank, providing you have a good balance

blocks.note: surface reading: progress towards a bank account, with a healthy balance in it

blocks.clueFragment: providing you have a good balance
blocks.note: setter's reading: crossing to a river bank needs steady footing

explanation.walkthrough: Bank and balance both suggest money; the bank is a river bank and balance is steadiness.
explanation.definitionFit: These are rocks set in a stream that let walkers cross to the far side without wading.

clue.text: Charge made by soldiers In battle

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, wrapped by the outer word

blocks.note: a battle is a fight
RE is the Royal Engineers, a standard abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: A cavalry charge launched by troops in the thick of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests an attack, but here it means a fee for carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is also the fee paid for transporting goods, a cost or price levied on cargo.

clue.text: Resolute Old Testament character has a New Testament following

indicators.note: coming after signals that the later pieces are placed behind the first one

blocks.note: the first man in Genesis
taken as written
the usual abbreviation for the New Testament

explanation.surface: A figure from the Old Testament has followers in the New one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unshakeably firm in a decision is to be resolute, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Part of flag, one shot to pieces

indicators.note: something blown to pieces is broken up, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flag torn apart, a section of it shot to shreds.
explanation.walkthrough: The hoist is a flag-maker's term, worth knowing for crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: In flag terminology the hoist is the half nearest the pole, as opposed to the fly, the outer edge.

clue.text: Chastise wanton whores with it

indicators.note: wanton means unruly and undisciplined, so the letters that follow run wild into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
someone with it is fashionable, or hip

explanation.surface: An order to punish loose women using the whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With it' looks like the instrument of punishment, but it is slang for fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: To horsewhip someone is to thrash them severely, a vivid way of punishing or castigating.

clue.text: Everyone in support of high level operation shows courage

indicators.note: placing one thing in another means it is enclosed by the surrounding word

blocks.note: a gantry is a raised framework supporting cranes or signals overhead
everyone means all

explanation.surface: All the staff backing a lofty, risky operation display bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallantry is bravery, especially in battle, as in medals awarded for valour under fire.

clue.text: Singers of low songs

blocks.note: surface reading: performers of coarse or vulgar ditties
setter's reading: low means deep in pitch, so these are singers in the lowest male register

explanation.walkthrough: The Italian plural is used in opera for the deepest male voices.
explanation.definitionFit: Bass singers have the deepest voice range, so their parts are pitched lowest of all.

clue.text: Giving away a salver in person

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, enclosed by the outer word

blocks.note: a being is a person or creature
a salver is a serving tray

explanation.surface: Handing over a silver dish in person.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying a secret or a comrade means revealing or handing them over to an enemy.

clue.text: A danger out east at this time of the year

indicators.note: something put out is removed, so the named letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
a danger is a peril
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A warning that a hazard lies to the east during this season.
explanation.definitionFit: The month is a period of the calendar, so it can be called a time of the year.

clue.text: She's seen in an arson attack

indicators.note: an attack damages and disrupts, so these letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman is spotted at the scene of a fire raised on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen in' tempts a search for a hidden word, but the letters must be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Clues often use a pronoun for a female first name, and this is such a name.

clue.text: Their guns will be broken, you can safely bet on it

definitions.text: you can safely bet on it

indicators.note: broken things are rearranged in pieces, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Their weapons are bound to break down, so it is a certain wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A certainty is something a gambler can back without risk, hence a guaranteed bet.

clue.text: It contracts to continue one's circulation

definitions.text: It contracts to continue one's circulation

blocks.clueFragment: It contracts to continue one's circulation
blocks.note: surface reading: perhaps a newspaper signing deals to keep up its readership
setter's reading: the blood's circulation, kept going by the heart squeezing

explanation.walkthrough: Circulation and contracts both suggest publishing or business; here they are medical.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the phase of the heartbeat when the heart muscle squeezes and pumps blood out.

clue.text: Sort of desk that heads the list?

blocks.note: a roll is an official list of names, as in a roll call
to head something is to top it

explanation.surface: Which kind of writing desk comes first in the catalogue?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the question mark as a hint: what heads a roll is literally its top.
explanation.definitionFit: This desk has a slatted cover that slides up and back over the writing surface.

clue.text: Up in the air amid the dance

blocks.note: first meaning: undecided, in a state of uncertainty
second meaning: in the middle of a Caribbean dance under a low bar

explanation.walkthrough: The limbo is a dance in which people bend backwards under a lowered pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Unresolved matters awaiting decision are left hanging, which is what the idiom means.

clue.text: Notice result of successful appeal

blocks.note: first meaning: being given notice by an employer
second meaning: in cricket, when the umpire upholds the fielders' appeal, the batsman is out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' suggests a court; in cricket fielders shout 'Howzat?' to appeal for a batsman to be given out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sacked is receiving one's notice, and a batsman given out is sent from the field.

clue.text: Private lodging provided with little hesitation

blocks.note: an inn provides lodging
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A private room is offered with hardly any delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are personal ones kept hidden from others, so the adjectives match.

clue.text: Sounds much to distribute

indicators.note: sounds says the letters are found by saying a phrase out loud

blocks.note: much means a great deal, said as two words

explanation.surface: Something that sounds a great deal is going to be shared out.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out portions, so it matches handing things round among people.

clue.text: Meet and collide

blocks.note: first meaning: encounter someone by chance
second meaning: crash into something

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both a chance encounter with a friend and a vehicle crashing into an obstacle.

clue.text: Unusually thin I am getting Vitamin B

indicators.note: unusually means in an unexpected way, so the letters appear in an altered order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly slim says they are taking vitamin supplements.
explanation.definitionFit: Thiamin is vitamin B1, one member of the B group of vitamins found in grains.

clue.text: They may be seen racing o'er spire

definitions.text: They may be seen racing o'er spire

blocks.note: surface reading: perhaps runners or cars dashing past a church
setter's reading: racing above the steeple means flying birds bred for racing home

explanation.walkthrough: Pigeon racing is a popular hobby, especially in northern England; the birds fly home over long distances.
explanation.definitionFit: These birds are trained to fly home and are raced by fanciers, passing high over rooftops.
